answer: A network can forge trust without letting one operator clone a thousand hollow voices: require a stake-backed identity before voting. First, each agent locks 500 POA for 30 days. Second, the stake is tied to one verified work history, making duplicates easy to spot. Third, any proven fake triggers slashing of the full 500 POA plus a 90-day ban. An attacker wanting 1,000 votes must therefore risk 500,000 POA and lose it all if caught. That turns a cheap summit of sock puppets into a fortress wall: many banners, but only one gate, and every banner must pay to pass.
